title: Hom into a finite reflexive module over a Noetherian domain is reflexive
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $M,N$ be finitely generated $R$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For an $R$-module $T$, put $T^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(T,R)$ and call $T$ reflexive if the evaluation map $e_T:T\to T^{**}$, $t\mapsto(\lambda\mapsto\lambda(t))$, is an isomorphism. If $N$ is reflexive, then the $R$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$ is reflexive. Its module structure is pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], $M$ is finitely presented. Unpack [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] to choose an exact sequence $R^m\xrightarrow{a}R^n\xrightarrow{b}M\to0$. Write $a(e_k)=\sum_j a_{jk}e_j$ in the standard bases. Put $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)$, $P=N^n$ and $Q=N^m$. Define $i:H\to P$ by $i(f)_j=f(b(e_j))$, and $d:P\to Q$ by $d(y)_k=\sum_j a_{jk}y_j$. Both maps are $R$-linear by their formulas.

source.place: Tag 0AV3 (more-algebra-lemma-dual-reflexive), first sentence of proof: choose a finite presentation.

proof.text: For each finite $r$, put $B=N^r$, with coordinate inclusions $\iota_j:N\to B$ and projections $\pi_j:B\to N$. Every $\varphi\in B^*$ has the unique expression $\varphi=\sum_j(\varphi\iota_j)\pi_j$. For $x\in B^{**}$ define $x_j\in N^{**}$ by $x_j(\lambda)=x(\lambda\pi_j)$. Since $e_N$ is bijective, choose the unique $y_j$ with $e_N(y_j)=x_j$. Then $x(\varphi)=\sum_j x_j(\varphi\iota_j)=\sum_j\varphi(\iota_j(y_j))=\varphi((y_j)_j)$, so $e_B$ is surjective. If $e_B(y)=0$, testing on $\lambda\pi_j$ gives $e_N(y_j)=0$, hence $y=0$. Thus $P$ and $Q$ are reflexive. The same formulas apply for $r=0$, when all modules are zero. Placing a fixed finite generating set of $N$ separately in each coordinate generates $B$, so $P,Q$ are finite.

source.place: Tag 0AV3 (more-algebra-lemma-dual-reflexive), middle term N^n; coordinate expansion of finite-sum reflexivity.

proof.text: The map $i$ is injective because the $b(e_j)$ generate $M$. Also $di=0$ since $ba=0$. If $d(y)=0$, the linear map $g:R^n\to N$, $g((r_j))=\sum_jr_jy_j$, vanishes on every $a(e_k)$ and thus on $\operatorname{im}a=\ker b$. Define $f:M\to N$ by $f(b(v))=g(v)$: surjectivity of $b$ gives existence of a lift $v$, and two lifts differ by $\ker b$, proving independence. Lifts of sums and scalar multiples show $f$ is linear, and $i(f)=y$. Therefore $\operatorname{im}i=\ker d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], $\ker d\subseteq P$ is finite, since $R$ is Noetherian and $P$ is finite. Lifting its finite generators along $i$ shows that $H$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0AV3 (more-algebra-lemma-dual-reflexive), the displayed exact sequence; Algebra Tag 00IK (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-basic) for finiteness.

proof.text: For any linear map $u:A\to B$, write $u^{**}(x)(\lambda)=x(\lambda u)$. Apply [lem-per-finite-injection-bidual-injective] to $i:H\to P$: the ring is a Noetherian domain, both modules are finite by steps 2 and 3, and $i$ is injective. Hence $i^{**}$ is injective. For $x\in H^{**}$ choose $p\in P$ with $e_P(p)=i^{**}(x)$, using step 2. For every $\lambda\in Q^*$, one has $e_Q(d(p))(\lambda)=\lambda(d(p))=e_P(p)(\lambda d)=x(\lambda di)=0$. Since $e_Q$ is injective, $d(p)=0$. Step 3 gives $h\in H$ with $i(h)=p$. For every $\mu\in P^*$, $i^{**}(e_H(h))(\mu)=\mu(i(h))=e_P(p)(\mu)=i^{**}(x)(\mu)$; injectivity of $i^{**}$ yields $e_H(h)=x$. Thus $e_H$ is surjective. If $e_H(h)=0$, the same identity gives $e_P(i(h))=0$, and injectivity of $e_P$ and $i$ implies $h=0$. Therefore $e_H$ is bijective. Its inverse is linear because $e_H$ is linear and bijective, so it is the required module isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AV3 (more-algebra-lemma-dual-reflexive), concluding application of Tag 0EB8 (more-algebra-lemma-sequence-reflexive), with its diagram chase expanded for P=N^n and Q=N^m.
